messages:
Anya K: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal for a cohesion-first decomposition roadmap. I put notes + rough cutover plan here: https://go.redwood/rfc/cohesion-first (TL;DR: split services by domain invariants and single-writer aggregates rather than current repo/module boundaries). Need opinions on DB ownership, read-model denorm, and safe rollout steps.

Mike R: Quick Q — by "single-writer aggregates" do you mean each aggregate gets a dedicated write service + DB shard? how do we handle joins across aggregates for historical queries?

Anya K: yeah — one service owns mutate operations for an aggregate and its write model. For cross-aggregate historical joins we keep an events-based materialization + denormalized read stores (event-sourced-ish for paydown). idea is: write-side consolidation, read-side duplication. minimizes write contention and lets teams own contracts.

Seun A: sounds reasonable but duplication = more ops cost. we should estimate storage + pipeline cost before committing. also worried about eventual consistency surprises for product teams. need SLOs on staleness.

Anya K: agreed on cost & staleness SLAs. Rough plan: phase 0 = identify 6 low-risk aggregates to prototype, estimate storage/ETL cost; phase 1 = build materializers + readonly denorms with 1m staleness SLO; phase 2 = canary traffic rewrite for reads; phase 3 = cutover writes once validation passes.

Olivia P: +1. For validation we should have automated contract checks and a lightweight end-to-end harness that runs golden prompts and sample queries. Example compatibility test (pseudo):

```yaml
contract_check:
  - name: create-user-aggregate
    request: { path: "/users", method: POST, body: {name: "test"} }
    expected: { status: 201, schema: {id: string, created_at: string} }

  - name: read-user-profile
    request: { path: "/profiles/123", method: GET }
    expected: { status: 200, schema: {id: string, name: string, last_active: string} }
```

Olivia P: We should run that in CI against both old and new read stores during canary window. If mismatch > 0.1% for critical fields, rollback.

Mike R: what about transactional concerns? e.g., a request that needs to update two aggregates atomically. Are we OK with sagas or must support distributed transactions?

Anya K: prefer sagas/orchestration; distributed tx adds operational fragility. For a few rare cases we can provide a coordinator service that wraps both writes and exposes a compensated API, but we should avoid making that the default. Document patterns in the RFC.

Seun A: rollout cadence idea: do one proto-service for the ingestion path (low-latency, idempotent ops) then tackle conversational-state aggregates next (higher risk). Also we should measure tail-latency impact when we add materializers (streaming vs batch).

Anya K: good call. I'll add a measurement checklist: baseline tail p99 for write path, latency added by materializer (<10ms target for streaming), and end-to-end read tail for canary.

deployment-bot: Reminder: prototype infra workspace for "cohesion-proto" will be provisioned tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Use the infra-ephemeral tags and destroy after 72h.

Olivia P: one more ops ask — add observability hooks for contract drift: schema diffs + field-level error rates. we can surface in console as "breaking field" alerts so teams see regressions early.

Anya K: will do. Next steps: 1) I'll post an updated RFC with prototype targets and a cost estimate template by EOD Wed. 2) @Mike R and @Olivia P — can you volunteer to own the canary checklist? 3) @Seun A — can you run a quick cost-ballpark for denorm storage and streaming infra?

Mike R: happy to own the canary checklist.

Olivia P: I can own the contract/CI work.

Seun A: will run numbers tomorrow and post in thread.

Anya K: thanks all — will update RFC and tag infra once prototype workspace is ready. :thumbsup:
